paper.title: Group-Fair Online Allocation in Continuous Time

settings.name_in_paper: Continuous-time online learning for group-fair utility maximization with deadlines (delayed full-information feedback)
unmapped: Actions are (group, deadline) pairs from [K] x finite deadline set {t_1..t_L}
Each task consumes random completion time min{X, deadline} from a total time budget B; process stops when budget exceeded
Objective is sum of concave utilities U_k of per-group reward rates (fairness), not total reward
Rewards R_{k,n}(t) in [0, R_max(t)], positive completion times
Full-information feedback revealed with constant delay tau
settings.definition_quote: If an individual from group $k\in[K]$ is chosen for the $n$-th task, he/she takes $X_{k,n}$ units of completion time ... reward of $R_{k,n}(t)=\overline{R}_{k,n}\mathbb{I}\{X_{k,n}\leq t\}$ ... We assume a delayed full-information feedback model where the completion time and reward of all groups for task $n$ are revealed to the controller at stage $n+\tau$

conditions: comparator is the best stationary randomized policy (Pi_S)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: For any $V>0$ and constant delay $\tau$, the regret under $\pi^{\tt OLUM}$ is bounded as ${\tt REG}_{\Pi_S}{^{\pi^{\tt OLUM}}}(B) = O\Big(\sqrt{\frac{\log(B)}{B}} + \frac{V}{B}+\frac{1}{V}\Big).$

results.notes: Regret is the utility gap OPT - U^pi of time-averaged reward rates (not a cumulative regret), so it was not multiplied by B: utility is nonlinear. Instance-dependent constants are hidden in O.

conditions: comparator is the best stationary randomized policy (Pi_S)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: By choosing $V = \Theta(\sqrt{B/\log(B)})$, we obtain ${\tt REG}_{\Pi_S}{^{\pi^{\tt OLUM}}}(B) = O(\sqrt{\log(B)/B})=\tilde{O}(1/\sqrt{B})$.

results.notes: Tuning V needs B, so the horizon (budget) is treated as known. Regret is on time-averaged utility and was not rescaled.
